A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MeCo research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A-D. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of all material.

before.justification: v2 reports original pre-training, conditional-inference, toxicity, and ablation experiments, including detailed results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results, including the main comparisons and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The metadata-conditioned training stage, standard-text cooldown, loss masking, architecture, and conditional-inference procedure remain unchanged in Section 2 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4, RefinedWeb, and DCLM, the same ten downstream tasks, and the same conditional-generation toxicity scenarios. Appendix coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including standard pre-training, fastText data selection, and 240B-token standard training in Table 1. The added related-work citations introduce no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Model sizes, training budgets, data handling, OLMES evaluation settings, and toxicity-sampling procedures are unchanged, including the settings in Appendix A.

E4.justification: The data-mixing and metadata-type ablations in Section 5, cross-document-attention analysis in Appendix B.1, and cooldown-length ablation in Appendix B.3 are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Both disclose single main runs and retain Appendix B.2's three training continuations from one 90%-trained baseline checkpoint. The standard-deviation reporting in Table 13 is unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported results match, including appendix tables and graphical results. For example, Table 1 retains average accuracies of 55.7% for 160B-token standard training, 56.7% for 160B-token MeCo, and 56.7% for 240B-token standard training.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised. The new Section 6 paragraph summarizes theoretical studies by other authors without adding mathematical development to this work.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about data efficiency, steerability, and compatibility with different metadata types. The priority claim concerning modern-scale language-model pre-training also retains its meaning.

C2.justification: The document-grouping interpretation, proposed mechanism hypotheses, and limitations remain unchanged. These include English-only experiments, unstudied interactions with post-training, and incomplete mechanistic understanding.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains identical hyperparameters, model configurations, cooldown details, GPU resources, and prompts. The model, data, and code access statement on page 1 is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds citations and brief summaries of Zhu et al. (2025) on context-enhanced learning and Wang et al. (2025) on conditional generative modeling as concurrent work. This modestly expands research positioning while preserving the central novelty claim.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short related-work paragraph and lightly edits the adjacent positioning statement. It also updates the arXiv version stamp and the Wettig et al. (2025) reference from a preprint to ICML publication details; the overall narrative and section structure remain stable.

P2.justification: The added paragraph causes limited text reflow, moving Acknowledgments from PDF page 10 to page 11 and shifting bibliography content. Figures 1-6 and Tables 1-21 are visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves research context and attribution by acknowledging and summarizing two concurrent studies absent from v2's discussion. The methodology, empirical evidence, appendices, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall quality gain is limited.
